newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP demands strict control over gene experiments.
newsitem.headline: EP demands strict control over gene experiments.

text.p: The European Parliament demanded stricter safety rules on Wednesday for laboratories experimenting with the genetic make-up of dangerous micro-organisms such as the AIDS or Ebola viruses.
The parliament adopted a report insisting that the European Commission tighten up the safety aspects of proposed legislation on genetically modified micro-organisms (GMMs).

The proposal would update existing European Union rules to take account of progress in the biotechnology sector. But it would downgrade the risk classification of micro-organisms such as AIDS, salmonella and tetanus viruses, making it easier for laboratories to obtain permission to experiment with them.

The parliament said that while it was important to encourage progress in biotechnology, a promising new European industry facing fierce competition from the United States, this should not be at the expense of human safety or the environment.
They proposed amendments to introduce clear guidelines for judging the risk posed by specific micro-organisms and stricter authorisation procedures for those in the high risk categories.
The parliament also demanded that labs experimenting with GMMs be fully liable for any accident which harmed humans, animals or the surrounding environment.
They should also "avoid", rather that "limit", as the Commission suggested, the release of any GMMs into the wild.
"Safety is paramount for the expansion of this technology," Greek deputy Antonios Trakatellis, who is in charge of the legislation, told reporters after the vote.
Even a single accident could cause public panic similar to that provoked by the mad cow crisis.
The rules must ultimately be adopted by EU ministers.
